w: At 6.50 a.m. Swamishri performed the foundation - stone laying ceremony for the new assembly hall in Surendranagar. After performing his puja, Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha of Ghanshyam Maharaj in the mandir shrine at 8.00 a.m. In his blessing s thereafter, he said, "Now that the murti of Ghanshyam Maharaj has been consecrated, He will bless and make everyone happy in the region of Jhalavad ... Make a point to come here for darshan once a day. Keep Ghanshyam Maharaj in your heart. He will fulfill your wishes. The murti is very beautiful and divine..."

An assembly to mark the murti-pratishtha ceremony and the 53rd anniversary of Swamishri's presidentship of BAPS commenced at 8.00 a.m. After speeches and bhajans, the Collector of Surendranagar Shri Dharaiya spoke laudingly of Swamishri's socio-spiritual works. Thereafter Swamishri was honored with garlands and a shawl. Finally Swamishri blessed the assembly, "The murti of God has been installed here today. By doing darshan of God's murti you will experience inner peace. Your thoughts will become calm and your miseries will be dissolved. When you stand before Him with inner love, devotion and chant His name then your wishes will be fulfilled..."

At 5.05 p.m., Swamishri departed from Surendranagar and arrived in Bochasan for darshan of Thakorji at 7.10 p.m. Thereafter Swamishri left for Atladra and arrived at 8.15 p.m. The students at PIIT alongwith their computer studies are also encouraged and educated in management, communication, leadership and teamwork skills. The chief guest of the function was the Additional Secretary from the Central IT Ministry of India Shri Laxminarayanan and Dr. Madhu Mehta. Both praised Pramukh Swami Maharaj's efforts in producing professionals wedded to our cultural values and ideals. The students graduating from B-level (MCA) in PIIT were presented with certificates from Shri Laxminarayanan. In conclusion, Swamishri blessed the assembly by elaborating upon God's power being the root of all our progress.
Parents’ Day
Senator of Cherry Hill, Jhon Adler, received Swamishri’s blessings.

The Mayor of Woodbridge, Frank Pelzman, received Swamishri’s blessings. During his address on the previous day he said, “I am so moved by the sincerity, devotion and the love that is in this room. I only hope that the job that I do as Mayor has his (Swamishri’s) blessings and has your (audiences’) prayers to help and guide me over the next 5 years of my term. So, I ask you, please remember me in your prayers that I do what is right for most of the people in our town.”

Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of pujan and arti for ten BAPS hari mandirs: Rohina – Beda Faliya, Vankacch, Raabdi, Nana Vaghchhipa, Ugta – Panva, Kharedi, Mankadban, Kurgam – Tumbi, Tadfaliya – Pardi, and Bhutsar.

During the meal, while the "Swaminarayan Prakash" was being read, the topic of family unity and family values came up. Aksharvatsal Swami said, "In this year's American presidential election, one candidate has made it an issue that they will make efforts to increase family unity."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj immediately asked, "What efforts will they make?"
Aksharvatsal Swami said, "It is an election issue, but there was not much talk of what they will actually do."
"Have they done any such work?"
"No, just talk," said Hari (Dallas).

Swamishri said, "It is just talk, for votes. Until spirituality comes into a person, a feeling for the family will not come either. Whatever laws they make, it still will not come. If it is not in their own home, what can they give to others?"
Mahendrabhai Barrister said, "At the most, the government might make a law to keep the tax lower for joint families and higher for separate families."

Swamishri said, "What will reducing tax do? Will it bring minds together? If tax is reduced, money will be saved, and instead they will spend more on pleasures. To bring minds together, spirituality is needed."

Pramukh Swami Maharaj was taking his walk. Meanwhile Amrutkirtan Swami sang the chesta (verses on the daily divine actions) of Shastriji Maharaj composed by Harikrishnadas Kothari. Swamishri became absorbed in the divine episodes of Shastriji Maharaj. During this singing, the walk came to an end. The machine was switched off. Swamishri was a little out of breath, and the singing of the chesta was still going on. But when the attendants said, "Finish now," Swamishri immediately said, "No, no, let me hear whatever is left."

Amrutkirtan Swami sang the kirtan until the verse was complete and finished it. Then Swamishri bent down a little, placed his whole hand on his head and said, "Wonderful! You let me hear the divine episodes of Shastriji Maharaj."

As Swamishri said these words, joy could be seen on his face as if he had met Shastriji Maharaj. His voice was breaking, yet as he stepped down from the machine Swamishri said, "Wonderful! Harikanda (Harikrishna)! Everything is in it."

In the evening, after finishing, Pramukh Swami Maharaj sat down to read letters. A youth had sent a 39 page letter. Swamishri calmly read the letter. Reading the letter took three quarters of an hour. After reading the letter, he spoke on the phone with the sadhu who travels in that area, who said, "Bapa! Did you read the whole letter?"
Swamishri said, "Only if we read it will we know, won't we!"
This is Swamishri's patience and his love for everyone.
At the end of a practical discussion, a sadhu said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "If I have displeased you, please forgive me."
Swamishri said, "When did you displease me? Give me the date." Having said this, Swamishri said, "I have not been displeased at all."
This is Swamishri's generosity.
Priyavardhan Swami, who had come from Sarangpur, spoke about his travels in the villages. Then he said, "We will never have to take the trouble that you have taken."

Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "I used to travel in this district every year. Since the time of Shastriji Maharaj, a festival was held on amas (new moon day) at Narayan Dhara in Acharada. We would hold the Shraddh festival in Sarangpur, come here, hold this festival and then travel on further."

ds.t: A fast for leaving Yogi Bapa
w: Today, when Mahant Swami Maharaj came to the sanctified room of Yogiji Maharaj, pointing to where the murti of Yogiji Maharaj is seated, he said:
"In summer, his (Yogiji Maharaj's) bed used to be here. His head would be towards the south. And I used to sleep right beside Yogi Bapa, on the right.

Once, in the afternoon, I felt very hot. There one could not cover oneself with a sheet, because it would feel even hotter, and if one did not cover oneself, the mosquitoes would bite. So I went outside and slept near the assembly hall. Yogi Bapa immediately came out and said to me, 'Am I to sleep alone? Why did you go away and leave me alone? A fast tomorrow!'"
Saying this, Swamishri burst out laughing. To Swamishri, this fast was like a priceless memory of his guru.

At the end of today's puja, after the prayer, the children started a dhun: "Swami and Narayan, Akshar and Purushottam, Brahma and Parabrahma, atma and Paramatma." In it, along with "Swami is Gunatit Swami, Narayan is Sahajanand Swami, Brahma is Gunatit Swami, Parabrahma is Sahajanand Swami," they also added, "Swami is Mahant Swami, Narayan is Sahajanand Swami, Brahma is Mahant Swami, Parabrahma is Sahajanand Swami."

After the puja was over, when Mahant Swami Maharaj went to the room behind to take his medicine, he said to the sadhus in charge of arrangements, "This dhun, Brahma and Parabrahma and so on: keep it pure. This never happened in the time of Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj or anyone."
Swamishri's plain meaning was that he did not at all like his name being added to this dhun. Then he also told Atmaswarupdas Swami to make an announcement about this.
"There are three kinds of listeners." With these words, Mahant Swami Maharaj began showering blessings after puja today:

"(1) One hears with one ear and lets it out of the other. (2) One hears and lets it out through the mouth, that is, one listens for others. (3) One hears with the ears and takes it into the heart. That is the best. We should become the third kind of listener.

Yogi Bapa used to say, 'We should become our own guru.' In short, we should keep whatever niyams we have taken. Shriji Maharaj says, 'My words are greater than my form.' Even if you are thousands of miles away, if you keep the niyams you are close. Make your upasana and your niyams firm. Reach that level. If there are these two, conviction and niyams, no one can stop you until you reach Akshardham, no one."

Mahant Swami Maharaj has a special liking for homoeopathic medicines. Today a doctor phoned about one such medicine. He began asking Swamishri questions in keeping with homoeopathic treatment. He asked, "Do you feel that a lot of responsibility has come upon you and that you are worried because of it?"
Swamishri naturally and clearly said "No."
He asked another question: "What do you like to do?"
Swamishri said, "Bhajan (devotion) and meeting devotees."
Swamishri's mind is constantly absorbed in Bhagwan and in devotion. That is why he has no tension or worry at all.

Today Acharya Dharmendraji, a well known speaker and a fervent promoter of Hinduism, came to meet Mahant Swami Maharaj. Acharya Dharmendraji recalled Pramukh Swami Maharaj in a touching way. Then, introducing Swamishri, Atmaswarupdas Swami told him, "Now the manifest guru, like the very form of Pramukh Swamiji Maharaj, is this Mahant Swami Maharaj."
Seeing Swamishri's health even at 83, Dharmendraji said, "Seeing him, my ego goes away, because he is healthier than I am."

Today Ghanshyamcharandas Swami said jokingly, "Hari tara naam chhe hajar, kaya naame lakhvi kankotri..." (O Hari, you have a thousand names; in which name should I write the invitation). Then, explaining the meaning, he said, "The place where you eat changes every day; how are we to know where to go?"
Narayanmunidas Swami laughed and said, "The description of Maharaj in the Vachanamrut is just like this, isn't it! He delivered the Vachanamruts in different places."

Mahant Swami Maharaj joined in, saying, "It says in the Vachanamrut, doesn't it, that Maharaj arrived and had his seat spread out and sat down; that is, it was not decided beforehand. Maharaj would go and decide. He would have his seat spread out and then the katha would begin."
Swamishri had given a hint.

Today Mahant Swami Maharaj came to the stage at the front of the Yagnapurush Sabha Mandap to bless the Children and Youth Day programme. The children began a game with Swamishri: "Passing the Ball," that is, passing a ball around while music plays. When the music stops, whoever has the ball in his hands is out. Then Swamishri would pick a slip, and the person would have to carry out whatever penalty came up!

The game began. In just the third round, Swamishri himself was out. Swamishri asked Doctor Swami to pick the slip with his penalty. Doctor Swami picked the slip, and on it was written: "Draw a picture giving a message to the children." Swamishri took the slate and pen in his hands and within moments drew a picture of a child doing dandvat (full prostration). Through it he inspired everyone to do dandvat.

As the programme went on, one child introduced himself, saying, "Swami! I am the atma. Do you recognise me? I am that devotee's boy whom you made repeat a hundred times, 'I am the atma, I am the atma.' I made a mistake that time, but now I will not make a mistake. Ask me and see."
Swamishri asked, "Who are you?"
The child said, "The atma."
"How?" Swamishri asked an unexpected second question.
The boy was ready too. He said, "Mahant Swami Maharaj is my atma." And then he requested, "Swami! Please make this firm in us."
Swamishri said, "I am the atma, the servant
of Bhagwan."
Swamishri taught the true way of reflecting on the atma: "Aksharam aham Purushottamadaso'smi" (I am Akshar, the servant of Purushottam).

Now the second half of the programme began. The youths presented a short skit and asked Mahant Swami Maharaj, "Swami! We keep niyams and do seva, yet the joy of satsang does not come like the joy of kesar mangoes. Please guide us on how it can come."
Giving the true understanding, Swamishri said:

"The joy of kesar mangoes means divine bliss. You will feel like following the commands of Maharaj and Swami and staying together. You will feel like doing satsang and doing seva. That is the joy of kesar mangoes you will get. On the day Pramukh Swami Maharaj was given the shawl (appointed president), he scrubbed pots. Is that not the joy of kesar mangoes? Could this happen without that feeling? Yogiji Maharaj did so much seva that he never even cut his nails. And Shastriji Maharaj would climb right into the big pots to do seva. Did that not bring the joy of kesar mangoes? This is the true meaning. Feeling like doing satsang. Running eagerly to satsang. When satsang remains foremost, it is said that the joy of kesar mangoes has come."
Swamishri gave a special definition: "the joy of kesar mangoes" means "feeling like doing satsang."
Today the sadhus who had come from Sankari told of an incident of Mahant Swami Maharaj's divine power:

"There was a pratishtha in the village of Lingad on the 18th. On the 15th we came to Ahmedabad to have the murtis consecrated by Swamishri. When we went back to Lingad, there was a tremendous wind there. The marquee had been torn to shreds. At night we phoned Swamishri. Swamishri was having his meal. Swamishri blessed us, saying, 'The wind will stop. There will be a supreme yagna and a supreme pratishtha.' Swamishri's blessings bore fruit. On the 16th everyone enthusiastically put up the marquee again. The wind stopped, and even the sun seemed to disappear. Clouds covered the sky. So the yagna and the procession through the town went very well. And on the 18th, the pratishtha by Ghanshyamcharandas Swami also took place supremely well, without any obstacle, just as Swamishri had said."
"Indra and the chief of sages keep trembling at his word,
The earth and the king of serpents keep trembling at his word;
The moon and the sun keep trembling at his word,
Night and day keep trembling at his word, ever at his service."
This was proved true on this occasion.
